messages:
Sam: FYI hit a weird blip in the handoff e2e: new shard prefetched a prefix, old node later completed a demote->evict and removed residency. the new owner briefly served stale entries then got evicted. small but visible 200ms tail on reads. anyone seen this ordering issue? :confused:
Rita: saw something like this in perf lab. sequence is: new prefetch wins window, writes residency; old hard-evict runs and deletes state; no fencing so new owner carries on until next confirm -> creates a tiny gap
Kai: we don't currently propagate a prefetch session id or any generation stamp with the prefetch stream. completion just writes residency unconditionally. that seems like the obvious weak point
Diego: two roads: add prefetch session gating (cheap on completion) or change eviction to a generation bump/tombstone owned by handoff coordinator. session gating seems lower-impact to reads
Sam: session gating idea: attach session_id + lease_epoch to prefetch stream header. completion handler does single compare against prefix.lease_epoch && session_id == active_session -> commit residency, else drop. no per-record CASs needed
Rita: agree. also add a short-lived "handoff marker" in prefix metadata created at demote start. completion must check marker epoch. that makes it explicit and traceable
Kai: we should also track metrics: kv.prefetch.session_aborts, kv.handoff.marker_collisions. alert if session_aborts ratio > 0.3% over 5m
Diego: about eviction generation: making hard-evict increment eviction_gen and write tombstone means stale prefetched residency will be ignored by readers. more durable but adds a small check in hot path. might be fine if we pack gen into 32-bit and check along with existing residency flags
Sam: thinking long-term: implement session gating first for quick mitigation, and behind a flag implement eviction_gen tombstones for added safety. hybrid: only emit tombstone if demote->hard-evict happens within Xs of demote (hand-off window). reduces metadata churn
Rita: also consider "sticky ownership" fallback: if a prefix has N aborted prefetches in short window, keep old owner sticky for S seconds to avoid oscillation. good for noisy hot prefixes
Kai: tests: unit for stale session completion (should not mark residency), integration where concurrent prefetch+evict race, and perf smoke for TTL on hot-read path with tombstone enabled
Diego: I'll prototype tombstone encoding: {evict_gen:uint32, tombstone_ts:uint64}. hard-evict increments evict_gen and writes tombstone. prefetch includes observed evict_gen; if tombstone.gen > observed -> abort. simple check
Sam: config knobs we want exposed to canary:
```
kv.prefetch.enable_session_gate=true
kv.handoff.marker_ttl_s=120
kv.eviction.gen_mode=opt_in  # none|opt_in|always
kv.eviction.gen_opt_in_window_s=45
kv.handoff.sticky_seconds=30
kv.prefetch.abort_alert_pct=0.3
```
Rita: ci-bot: please provision a 3-node canary with the above flags and a small tenant workload. aim: 10 prefixes with medium-hot read rate, run handoff churn script for 10m and check metrics/logs
ci-bot: requested canary created, config template posted to perms team
Kai: rollout plan: stage 1: session gating only (no gen tombstones), run canary, validate prefetch.session_aborts low and no read gaps. stage 2: opt-in gen mode for subset of prefixes, run perf numbers, ensure <1% overhead on hot path. stage 3: enable hybrid heuristics and sticky fallback if needed
Diego: rollback plan: session_gate=false, evict_gen=none, run cleanup to GC tombstones, revert canary images. list these in PRs
Sam: owners: Rita (session gating + marker + metrics), Diego (tombstone prototype + perf), Kai (tests + traces + alerting), Sam (canary orchestration + smoke harness). tag me on PRs and include rollback steps
Rita: will add trace spans: prefetch.session_id, prefetch.result, handoff.marker_epoch, evict.gen_before/after. makes console debugging straightforward
Kai: small optimization note: store evict_gen inline with prefix header to avoid extra memory lookups on read path. keep check a single branch on residency validation
Diego: I'll run microbench on 1M ops/s simulated reads and report overhead numbers for gen check and header packing
Sam: sounds good. follow-up: add an observability doc to the handoff runbook describing the new metrics and what thresholds mean
Rita: will do. closing thread once PRs link to issue. :white_check_mark:
